title: Compact batch state machine and modernize KV cache API
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
We will refactor the continuous batching state machine to a compact epoch-based coordinator and modernize the KV cache API to reduce lock contention, simplify async interactions, and remove a legacy LRU dependency. This is a targeted tech-debt effort intended to improve tail latency and reduce CPU usage on hot paths without changing public API semantics.

Motivation:
- Observed tail-latency spikes under high concurrency where batch state updates contend on a global mutex and KV cache reads cause short-lived stall cycles.
- Current batching state is spread across multiple mutable structs that are updated in different places which makes reasoning about lifetimes and lock ordering difficult.
- KV cache API is synchronous and tied to an older LRU implementation that does not support async warming/prefetch or efficient shard-local metrics.

Goals:
1) Replace scattered batch state with a compact epoch coordinator that owns per-lane epoch counters and a small immutable snapshot for readers. Expect ~15-25% reduction in mutex hold time in synthetic microbenchmarks.
2) Introduce an async-friendly KV cache interface (KvAsyncStore trait) and a small adapter that keeps the on-disk/legacy store compatible for migration.
3) Remove the old lru-cache crate from the hot path by swapping to a sharded concurrent bounded store; keep semantics identical for eviction behavior where feasible.
4) Upgrade tokio (runtime) and the tracing stack to the minimum versions required to support async cache warming APIs.
5) Add unit and integration tests, microbenchmarks, and canary rollout plan.

Non-goals:
- No changes to external client API or behavior of model serving routes.
- No immediate change to persistence format or long-term KV layout. Migration is in-place with adapters.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Step A (spike): Implement a prototype epoch coordinator in a sandbox crate, run under existing load tests to validate reduction in lock contention. (owner: Diego)
- Step B: Define KvAsyncStore trait with async get/put/evict/warm signatures; implement an adapter around existing KvStore to pass tests. (owner: Priya Mehta)
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests for epoch coordinator cover concurrent lane transitions and ensure no regressions in correctness.
- End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99 for sequence-length-128 synthetic workload shows no worse p50 and p99 improved by >=10% in the tail under 50% concurrency target.
- CI passes with tokio upgrade on Linux and Mac builders.
- Canary rollout (10% traffic) shows no error rate increase and lower CPU burn on serving nodes.
- Documentation: design doc linked, and internal API migration guide exists.
implementation_notes:
- Avoid introducing additional global locks; prefer per-lane atomics plus a single small snapshot protected by an RwLock.
- The KvAsyncStore adapter will delegate to the legacy store using spawn_blocking where required; long term we'll replace spawn_blocking callers with truly async IO-backed stores.
- We will use a feature flag (feature = "epoch-coordinator") to gate runtime behavior so we can flip during canary.
- Benchmark harness: extend bench/batching to measure hold-time of batch coordinator mutex and per-token CPU time.
- Rollout: dev -> staging -> canary (10%) -> gradual ramp if metrics stable.
- Keep a compatibility shim so Dedicated and Private customers remain on the same public API surface during rollout.
